description:
Programme or Project Overview

The University of Southampton recruits doctoral candidates to the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network BlueOcean, focused on robotic monitoring and data processing for seafloor change. The network develops autonomous platforms, sensing technologies and data pipelines to observe and understand seafloor dynamics - from habitat change to geohazards - training a cohort of doctoral researchers across European partner institutions. Applications close on 31 October 2026, so candidates should apply as early as possible.

MSCA doctoral candidates receive an attractive EU-funded package: a generous monthly living allowance (adjusted by the host country), mobility and family allowances where applicable, plus full coverage of research and training costs. Doctoral researchers must comply with the MSCA mobility rule - they may not have resided or carried out their main activity in the recruiting country for more than 12 of the 36 months before recruitment - and positions typically run for three years with international secondments.

Candidate profile and application

Applicants hold a master's degree (or equivalent) in robotics, computer science, electrical, mechanical or ocean engineering, or a related discipline, with interests in autonomous systems, sensing or marine data science. Applications are made through the University of Southampton's eRecruitment portal referencing vacancy 3522426DA, with a CV, transcripts, references and a motivation statement; shortlisted candidates are interviewed by the network's host groups.

Highlights

  • MSCA Doctoral Network BlueOcean - robotic seafloor monitoring
  • EU-funded allowance package with mobility terms
  • Autonomous platforms, sensing and data pipelines
  • International secondments across network partners
  • MSCA mobility rule applies
  • Closing date: 31 October 2026 - apply early

About University of Southampton

The University of Southampton is a Russell Group research university on England's south coast, ranking among the UK's top engineering, ocean and earth science institutions. It hosts the National Oceanography Centre partnership, world-leading maritime robotics groups and one of the UK's largest doctorate-training portfolios, including Marie Sklodowska-Curie doctoral networks. Southampton research spans engineering, environmental and marine sciences, electronics, health and the humanities, with doctoral candidates recruited through the university's eRecruitment portal for funded projects across its faculties and research institutes.
